blocks.title: Valence electrons
blocks.text: The electrons in an atom in the outermost shell are called valence electrons.

These are such electrons that are primarily involved in chemical reactions. The similarities among the configurations of valence electrons account for similarities of the chemical properties among groups of elements.
Figure 2.15 shows a periodic table which include the valence shell configurations included. Note the similarity in electron configuration within any group (column) of elements.

blocks.alt: A periodic table in which every box gives the atomic number, the symbol and that element's valence-shell configuration, from H 1s1 to Og 7s2 5f14 6d10 7p6, with the lanthanides Ce to Lu and actinides Th to Lr in two rows below. Colours mark the s block (pink), d block (light yellow-green), p block (green) and f block (lavender).
blocks.caption: Figure 2.15: The electronic distribution of elements of modern periodic table (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.15).
blocks.long_description: Each group shares one pattern: ns1 in group 1, ns2 in group 2, ns2 np1 to ns2 np6 in groups 13 to 18, and (n-1)d with ns in groups 3 to 12, with exceptions such as Cr 4s1 3d5, Cu 4s1 3d10, Nb, Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Ag, Pt and Au. The f rows fill 4f and 5f.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 2.15 has five slips: element 76 is printed 'Re' (it is Os); Tc is printed 5s¹ 4d⁶ (5s² 4d⁵), Pt 6s² 4f¹⁴ 5d⁹ (6s¹ 4f¹⁴ 5d⁹), Au 6s² 4f¹⁴ 5d¹⁰ (6s¹ 4f¹⁴ 5d¹⁰) and Yb 6s² 4f¹³ (6s² 4f¹⁴). They are drawn correctly above.
